description:
SYNTHETIC. Standard-library Python plus NumPy: symmetry entropy measures what a projection can resolve, what it must store, and what it is blind to. Four measured quantities: (1) orbit entropy log2(|orbit|) under the dihedral group D4 on 4x4 patterns -- asymmetric patterns 3 bits, blocks 1 bit, ring and cross 0 bits (orbit collapse, the falsified design); (2) projection entropy, the Shannon entropy of the Born weights after projecting onto a stored subspace -- 0 bits for a clean stored Bell state, 0.618 bits at noise sigma 0.25, 1.270 bits at sigma 0.75, 1.581 bits for a Haar-random state (max log2 3 = 1.585 bits); (3) asymmetry cost S(twirl(rho)) - S(rho) under the Pauli group {I, X} -- |0> costs 1 bit = log2(2), |+> costs 0 bits = log2(1); (4) self-determinism factor D = <psi|P|psi>, the squared norm of a probe's projection onto the stored subspace -- D = 1 for a clean stored probe, 0 for a kernel probe (Psi-, all Born weights 0), strictly between for noisy and random probes (Phi+ sigma 0.25: 0.843; sigma 0.75: 0.567; Haar-random mean over 200 seeds 0.720). D is the denominator of the Born weights. Four falsifiable claims, all measured: distinct recalls equal orbit size in closed-orbit mode; the projection kernel (Psi-, orthogonal to all stored patterns) is invisible with all Born weights 0; the projected world has higher entropy than the underlying state by the asymmetry cost, in the classical orbit case and the quantum twirl case; the projection is self-determined exactly to the extent the probe lies in the stored subspace. No headline claim is emitted. No speedup, no Bell violation, no hardware data, no claim about physical reality.

Acknowledgement: the vendored projection code derives from a package received under Mun Seok Lee's name (see the quantum-projection README Provenance section). No endorsement implied. Lee is inspiration only for the symmetry membrane.

title: Symmetry Entropy: orbit entropy, projection entropy, and asymmetry cost (SYNTHETIC classical emulation)
